name: issue-grinder
description: Deliver Task Manager scope, compose plans, and auto-review plans before launch or active long runs.

interface.shortDescription: Deliver scope; review plans before launch or active long runs.
interface.longDescription: Includes three independent Task Manager skills. Issue Grinder delivers an explicit issue, Release, Project, or current-Release scope through To Do, In Progress, and In Review. It also answers pure questions about its modes, default resolver, differences, or selection through a delivery-free help path that does not access Task Manager, create a Goal, rename the task, or call subagents. It supports four execution modes: Solo uses the current main profile without execution children; Classic keeps most implementation on its controller with independent Luna Max review; Balance requires a Luna Max main session, keeps coordination and ordinary implementation on Luna, and calls Sol Extra High for complex work and independent final review; Economical requires a Luna Max main session and uses Luna for substantive work and review, with an honest resumable checkpoint when needed. Explicit mode choice wins. Otherwise Luna Max selects Balance and Sol Extra High selects Classic regardless of task count. Other profiles retain Classic for non-Luna with multiple tasks and Solo otherwise. Economical is explicit-only. Balance and Economical refuse before effects or child dispatch when the actual main profile is not exactly gpt-5.6-luna/max, including on resume; a wrapper or supervisor cannot bypass this condition. The decision is made once per continuous run. Mode topology includes only agents doing Issue Grinder delivery work; outer controllers and bounded semantic providers stay outside it unless they take on analysis, implementation, testing, technical review, candidate selection, or delivery decisions. It creates a strategic Goal only for an explicitly invoked multi-issue run, keeps live scope dynamic, treats blocked-by as an implementation-readiness gate, and requires human-readable comments for every non-trivial lifecycle transition. Strategic Outcome stays present during implementation, delegation, review, blocker analysis, resume, and final reflection so local decisions serve the overall purpose. It never creates hidden requirements or new task debt: the formal completion condition remains a fresh empty active Task scope, even when the broader Strategic Outcome is only partially achieved. A candidate blocker must become a causal explanation and a fresh reflection over current primary sources; any verified safe in-scope action cancels the blocker and resumes work. A terminal handoff lists every confirmed blocking cause and gives a separate answer for each one explaining why it blocks the mandatory result of an active issue, why Issue Grinder cannot resolve it alone, and what the blocked step contributes to the issue contract and overall goal. Public UAT and other confirmed non-production environments do not need routine approval, while Production remains forbidden. Independent writers and recovery candidates use separate feature branches and Git worktrees, one integration owner performs fan-in, and final acceptance applies to one exact integrated candidate. Task Composer remains planning-only and creates Task Manager Backlog scope without implementing it. It keeps Strategic Outcome, protected Human Requirements, and the mutable Agent Plan distinguishable, projects relevant strategic context into child Tasks, and never promotes an agent assumption or optional hardening into a Human Requirement. All three skills use the separately installed Task Manager adapter. In all four modes Issue Grinder uses the standalone Strategic Explainer when available and otherwise writes natively; its provider remains outside mode execution topology while it handles only publication, and Explainer absence never blocks comments, status transitions, or final reporting. Scope Reviewer turns an exact selected plan or active Release into one human-readable report through separate fresh Luna Max perspectives. Plan review and every Release review remain read-only; explicit plan-improvement intent may change only the agent-owned planning model, never Human Requirements, delivery lifecycle, or working statuses. It reports formal Task completion separately from broader strategic achievement, and a strategic gap does not create a blocker, Task, or delivery loop. It uses the standalone Strategic Explainer when available and otherwise returns its own factual report with the missing editorial pass stated honestly.
defaultPrompt: Используй $issue-grinder, чтобы довести текущий Release в Task Manager до проверенного результата
Используй $issue-grinder:task-composer, чтобы оформить это требование в Task Manager Backlog
Используй $issue-grinder:scope-reviewer для ревью плана перед запуском или понятного обзора активного долгого Release.
